[h3] I'VE NEVER BEEN MORE STRESSED ABOUT DOTS ON A SCREEN [/h3] I've always wanted a game that feels like you're sitting at a Mother terminal in Alien commanding a squad. Xenopurge is that game. Really enjoy that the entire game can be played (and is recommended to) entirely with keyboard inputs. The game play loop is great, and I can finish a run in about 20 minutes. The loop is as follows: Start with your group of cloned troops > decide which track you want to follow on the map > Complete the missions and upgrade your troops/gear along the way. There is also metagame to add additional commands for your troops, gear, etc. Xenopurge is a perfect example of executing a simple formula to perfection. I look forward to seeing what the developer adds to the game in future. But, even as it stands, I'm happy with the amount of content in the game for the price.

Absolutely awesome real time tactics game! You can play it on an easy 'simulation' tactical pause mode, but I'd guess that would massively reduce the tension & excitement. I normally avoid real-time action in favour of proper turn based combat games. But this one is very much worth the effort. Getting snowball powerups with the bioweave squad and being totally OP for the second half of the run is the most fun I've had in years. Only -ve I'd call out is that they're being a bit naughty to call this is an auto-battler. Granted, it has auto-battler qualities and occasionally you get 40 seconds where you can just watch your squad take care of business. But mostly you need to micro manage with super quick reactions. I've even had the unexpected benefit of getting better at my job due to the mental exercise. Graphics are old school, but has near perfect sound & voice acting, also well written lore.

This is a very interesting game and I really enjoy the controls and squad management. I love the premise and there's a lot of potential here. I got my $12.50 of enjoyment out of it. Unfortunately the roguelike elements really detract from my enjoyment long term. I have unlocked untold guns, armor, and commands but I never get to use them because I have to randomly draw a store at a favorable part of the run where I might have resources and then the gear I want for my build has to be randomly offered. Resources are *extremely* scarce so on most runs I can afford one gun *or* one set of armor unless I get very lucky. I have started abandoning runs until I get a workable arrangement of stores. That's not fun. There's no discernible reward for progression. In fact the game seems to get harder. Some kind of squad customization where I can reconfigure before the run would make this a much more enjoyable game.

EDIT: Disabled comments as morons kept attempting to argue that this is an auto-battler, simply because the developers call it an auto-battler. In realty this is a limited control RTS with roguelite elements, but the few RTS controls you do get are so awful and non-specific that this game would honestly be better if the devs tossed the entire RTS aspect and actually made this an auto-battler. [hr][/hr] It's everything I never wanted from a RTS! It's quasi-turn based RTS with a significant lack of any true control over unit movement and roguelite elements that make this significantly RNG based. Possibly the worst top-down tactical RTS I've ever played. If the movement was similar to door kickers then I wouldn't even bother leaving a negative or positive review. Edit: I tried one more run to see if maybe unit control was an unlockable thing later on, but after one of my guys on recon came across a nest in a room with a powerful xeno and proceeded to target the nest instead of the guy murdering him, I rage quit. I am amazed that this is considered a finished game considering the "AI" considers a nest to be a higher targeting priority rather than an enemy that can deal damage.

Take control of the *dumbest* soldiers on in the galaxy? I know that this is a "guy in a chair" simulator, but I'm pretty sure the AI would need direct instructions on how to wipe. Average soldier: "Oh? Extract? I would, but unfortunately there is an alien down the opposite corridor, and even though I've had *direct instruction* to extract, I actually need to run into this end where I will be swarmed and killed. Don't worry though, Bishop will extract but... oh never mind, he decided to ignore all given commands and charge directly at a Queen!" I get that is supposed to build the tension of the Aliens scene where you see and can't directly communicate, but the Elite levels might as well be a roll of the dice. You're down to one guy? Sorry, but the care package is in the very last room, and now the waves actually make it impossible to extract with it *especially when extract seems to always be a suggestion*. It's fine as a concept, but the frustration is real. I've lost so many games to such *incredibly poor* AI. Sure, you 'can' change the action settings at various points in the game, even unlocking them as time goes on: But what is really the point when your men *actively ignore those choices*? Anyway; 4/10. Hope it'll be improved over time.

Great tactical snack game, and kind of what I hoped Aliens: Dark Descent would have felt like! I like that it starts pretty doable for a roguelike -- completing the first run isn't a great challenge but it slowly teaches you how the different commands and squad styles work. It has great atmosphere and does well at making you feel like a remote operator. The unlocks are smartly done; your commands start out pretty basic and you unlock more interesting things when you actually need them. I never felt like I had a lack of control. The progression/achievements feel a bit grindy with the "complete any combination of squads and runs" but so far, I'm having a lot of fun checking off said list. Definitely would recommend.

I really want to like this game but it falls short. Time is the enemy, aliens spawn increases with each wave. It pushes you to be as efficient as possible, to give commands quickly and correctly. It is suck when your soldiers die, but it pushes you to go for another run. Graphics are meh, but that's OK. Run times are short, about 10 mins or so. The game is repetitive but it tries to mix it up with different squads, random maps, weapons, armor, missions and commands. This is a rogue like so anything you buy gets wiped after every run. You can have a maximum of 4 soldiers. Your initial squad is always a mix of types. There are 3 types, but the only one that is useful is the "Stand and Fight" soldier. The other 2 will make you quit the game. "Stand" soldier will stop and then shoot when you see an alien. "Charge" will charge at an alien, no matter how far, will NOT shoot. "Fallback" soldier will run away from an alien and will ONLY shoot when it hits a wall. Later on in a mission, as aliens increase in numbers, it extremely hard to keep your people together. And you need to keep them together as waves go by. A soldier on their own later on a mission is a dead soldier. The trick is to know when to group up. You lose time as your soldiers have to waste it by grouping up after every battle. Later on a map you can upgrade the 2 crappy soldiers so they finally shoot while moving. It makes the 2 crappy soldiers slightly viable but they will still get your squad killed. You can also pick an initial squad with "upgraded logic" but again, it only makes the 2 crappy types slightly viable. I wish there was a way to change the initial soldiers types. I would pick only "Stand" soldiers. The path finding is mediocre. Sometimes they will slow down for no reason. This is especially so if you have 4 of them. Sometimes a soldier will decide to not recon a room it was designated (it is already at the door) simply because the recon assignments get switched after another finishes what they were doing. The mission types are good except for one. VIP missions. The VIP is slow. The VIP has no gun. Most importantly, the VIP will take up one of your 4 slots. Escort missions are the worst part in 99% of games. Xenopurge is part of the majority. It will make you check the randomly created maps and reroll if you can not find a way to avoid it. That's how horrible it is. Oh, minor gripe, but you can only "reroll" a map from the "Main Menu" screen. It is quick to do with mouse and keyboard. Just <ESC>, click, click. But with a gamepad, you have to press "Settings" button then scroll all the way down to select "Main menu", then "Start new run". It get's old when you want to reroll maps lots of times to avoid VIP missions. The weapons and armors/equipment are good, no complaints. Some have interesting advantages and disadvantages but they make sense. Like a heavy armor that will slow you down and lose accuracy. Or a shotgun with +dmg if an enemy is 1 tile away. There's these things in game called "Commands". You can buy them to expand what your soldiers can do in a run. I've only bought "Turret" and "Overwatch" commands. The other's seemed superfluous to me but I suspect it depends on your individual play style. Note that different squad types have different default commands and they will greatly influence how you play. After trying them out I find the most stable squad is the starting squad as they start with the limited use "Heal" and "Haste". Yes I know it is not called Haste. To summarize, the gameplay is great but it is greatly marred by being forced to use 2 crappy soldier types for "variety". What is frustrating is that if they only used "Stand and fight" soldier, it would make the game more fun. The pathing adds even more frustration when it causes undeserved loss. The frustration adds up to a point where it is no longer fun but torture. Oh, yes VIP missions. Even more torture. I'm going to uninstall the game. I have no idea if i will ever play it again. The good new is that I got it on sale so it does not hurt as much.
